**Finding: deviation (medium) — RENEWAL, at §2 (p0011) and §3(b) (p0014).**

What I found:

- **Renewal/exit limb — acceptable.** There is no auto-renewal anywhere in the document (no "renew" language at all). §2 is a simple evergreen term running "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6," and §6(a) permits either party to terminate for any or no reason on 15 days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding. That is easier to exit than our preferred 30-day opt-out, with no non-renewal notice window and no multi-year renewal term — nothing to walk away from here.
- **Pricing limb — fails.** Because the term rolls on indefinitely, §3(b)'s "Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company" operates as an uncapped, unlimited-frequency escalator, defeating the "priced predictably" half of the rule.

Redline (validated, ok:true): fix rates for the duration of each Statement of Work, and limit rate changes to once per 12 months on 60 days' written notice, capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% cap offered as fallback.
